title: choice.v1
description: One decision put to a person, in plain words, always as the same card (tools/render_page_tool.py): the question; why this person is asked and what they answered before, when either applies; the options explained in sentences; the options to select by number; a proposal when something decides one. Printed by agent/ask_person_tool.py — in the terminal, or in Markdown with a box per option on the code host — never written by hand. No requirement ID in the words: the person reads them without the requirements open.

question.description: One question, ending with '?': 'What happens when the user enters a wrong password?'

why_you.description: Why this person is asked, in one plain sentence: the critical requirement it touches, or what else makes it theirs to decide: 'A security requirement changed: publishing now sends the site's password with every retry.'

before.description: What the person already answered on the same matter, when they did: 'On 2026-10-21 you answered: retry once, then tell the editor.' It shows that nothing is asked twice.

options.description: The options explained in sentences: 'We could block the account immediately, or give the user two more chances.'

select.description: The options as short labels, numbered from 1 in this order: the person answers with a number.

proposal.description: The option proposed and why; the person accepts it with Y. Left out when nothing decides one.
